(Capacity: 19,368) |tourney= [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result= Elite Eight }} {{2020-21 Southeastern Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2020–21 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Arkansas]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team was led by second-year head coach [[Eric Musselman]] and played its home games at [[Bud Walton Arena]] in [[Fayetteville, Arkansas]], as a member of the [[Southeastern Conference]]. The Razorbacks finished second in the SEC regular season and earned a 3 seed in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament's]] South Regional. Arkansas went on to make it to the Sweet Sixteen of the NCAA Tournament for the first time since the [[1995–96 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|1995–96 season]], and then to the Elite Eight for the first time since the [[1994–95 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|1994–95 season]]. Freshman guard [[Moses Moody]] was named the SEC Freshman of the Year, 1st Team All-SEC, Freshman All-American, and [[Associated Press|AP]] Honorable Mention All-American. The Razorbacks finished the season with an overall record of 25–7, 13–4 in SEC play, and finished ranked #6 in the [[Coaches Poll]] and #10 in the [[AP Poll]]. Arkansas's season ended when they lost to eventual national champion [[2020–21 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] in the Elite Eight. ==Previous season== The [[2019–20 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|Razorbacks]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] with a record of 20–12, 7–11 in SEC play to finish in a tie for 10th place. Junior [[Mason Jones (basketball)|Mason Jones]] won a share of the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] award and was named a consensus First-Team All-SEC player.{{Cite web|url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/mar/10/mason-jones-named-ap-co-sec-player-year/|title = Mason Jones named AP Co-SEC player of the year}} Arkansas started the season strong, going into conference play with an 11–1 record, including two road wins against Power Five teams, Georgia Tech and Indiana. After winning their first-round game against Vanderbilt on March 11, 2020, the Hogs were slated for a rematch against South Carolina in the second round, but the SEC announced on March 12, 2020 that the SEC Tournament was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], with an announcement following from the NCAA later that day that the whole tournament was cancelled, along with all other winter and spring championships, ending the Razorbacks' season. They finished with 20 wins against 12 losses in coach Eric Musselman's first season. He was the first coach to win 20 games in his initial campaign at Arkansas since [[John Pelphrey]] won 23 in the [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08 season]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.hogstats.com/results.php|title=HogStats.com :: Year-by-Year Results|website=www.hogstats.com|accessdate=March 19, 2023}} ==Offseason== On August 1, 2020, star guard [[Isaiah Joe]] announced that he was withdrawing his name from the [[2020 NBA draft]] and returning for his junior season.{{cite news |last1=Holt |first1=Bob |title=Joe makes call to remain Hog |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/aug/02/joe-makes-call-to-remain-hog/ |accessdate=August 3, 2020 |publisher=WholeHogSports |date=August 2, 2020}} Joe was a member of the 2019 SEC All-Freshman Team and earned preseason All-SEC recognition prior to his [[2019-20 Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball team|sophomore season]], before going on to lead the league in three-pointers made, rank fourth in the NCAA for three-pointers made per game, as well as being named SEC Player of the Week on December 30, 2019 before having knee surgery on February 4, 2020, which sidelined him for six games.{{cite web |title=Isaiah Joe |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/isaiah-joe/ |website=Arkansas Razorbacks |date=July 16, 2018 |publisher=University of Arkansas |accessdate=August 3, 2020}} Joe would have highlighted a group of three returnees with starting experience for the Hogs, but on August 17, 2020, sixteen days after his initial announcement, Joe reversed his decision and opted to declare for the 2020 NBA draft.{{cite news |last1=Bordelon |first1=Scottie |title=Isaiah Joe re-entering 2020 NBA Draft |url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/aug/17/isaiah-joe-re-entering-2020-nba-draft/ |accessdate=August 20, 2020 |agency=WholeHogSports |publisher=Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Inc. |date=August 17, 2020}} ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
